sections.h2: Which offices handle taxes for a Fort Lauderdale home?
sections.html:
Fort Lauderdale sits in Broward County, so the county property appraiser sets your value and the Broward tax collector sends the bill.

The Broward County Property Appraiser's Office takes calls at 954-357-6830 and lists weekday hours of 8 am to 5 pm. The Fort Lauderdale city home page carries a feature on how property taxes and other locally raised revenue support public safety, roads, parks and neighborhood infrastructure, which is a useful read for seeing where the city's portion goes.

sections.h2: What does the Census show about Fort Lauderdale housing?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists a July 2025 population estimate of 188,677, a gain of 3.3 percent over the 2020 base, and 80,999 households across 2020 to 2024.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 54.1 percent.
  • Typical owned home value: $486,700.
  • Owner costs each month: $2,679 with a mortgage, $1,122 without.
  • Median gross rent: $1,854.
  • Share of residents 65 and over: 19.6 percent.

Those figures matter for taxes because older owners may qualify for the extra senior exemption described below, and because nearly half the city's homes are rented rather than owner-occupied.

sections.h2: Which dates matter to a Fort Lauderdale owner?
sections.html:
Dates follow the statewide calendar, and Broward adds its own filing windows for exemptions.

Property tax calendar for Fort Lauderdale owners, from state and Broward appraiser pages
WhenWhat happens
January 1Value is set, and permanent residence is judged as of this date
March 1Exemption applications due on time
AugustNotice of Proposed Property Taxes (TRIM) is mailed
Within 25 days of that noticePetition on value due with the clerk
NovemberTax bills go out; 4 percent discount for paying in November
April 1Unpaid taxes become delinquent

The state also prints discounts of 3 percent in December, 2 in January and 1 in February.

sections.h2: How does the Broward homestead exemption work for a Fort Lauderdale home?
sections.html:
Broward's appraiser says the basic homestead exemption saved a county homeowner in 2026 between $673 and $1,020, depending on the city's millage rate, on homes valued at $75,000 or more.

Qualification turns on residence status on January 1. The appraiser requires a Florida driver's license or state ID, plus either Florida voter registration or a power or water bill in an owner's name. If the property is in a trust, bring a notarized certificate of trust or the full trust. For 2027, the on-time window ran March 3, 2026 to March 1, 2027, and late filing ends September 20, 2027. The 2026 late-filing window closed September 18, 2026.

sections.h2: What other relief is available in Fort Lauderdale?
sections.html:
Broward lists several, each with its own paperwork.

  • Additional low-income senior exemption: age 65 or older on January 1, homestead on the property, and household income under the cap, which the appraiser printed as $38,686 for last year's income with a yearly cost-of-living adjustment. File January 1 through March 1 each year.
  • $5,000 exemptions for disability, blindness and widowed persons.
  • $5,000 veteran's disability exemption, and full exemption for a veteran's total and permanent service-connected disability.
  • Granny flat exemption for permitted additions housing a parent or grandparent aged 62 or older, up to 20 percent of homestead value.
  • Historic property exemptions.

Call 954-357-6830 for details on any of these.

sections.h2: How do I contest my Fort Lauderdale assessment?
sections.html:
A value challenge is a petition to the clerk, due 25 days after the August notice. If an exemption was denied, the value adjustment board hears it, on a 30 day clock from the denial letter.

Broward's Records, Taxes and Treasury division supports the Value Adjustment Board, which settles disagreements between taxpayers and the appraiser over exemptions, classifications and valuations. The board's office is at 1801 NW 49th Street, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33309, reachable at 954-357-7205 or 954-357-5444, with hours of 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Start with a phone call to the appraiser, since many errors are fixed informally.

sections.h2: How do the state caps limit increases on a Fort Lauderdale bill?
sections.html:
Two limits keep assessed value from jumping with the market. Homestead value under Save Our Homes rises by no more than 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is lower; the state's chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026.

Rentals and second homes face a looser ceiling of 10 percent a year. Both limits reset when the property changes hands, which is why a Fort Lauderdale buyer's first bill can look very different from the seller's. The state also says the basic homestead exemption is up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 applying to school taxes and the second slice reaching only non-school taxes.

sections.h2: What should a Fort Lauderdale seller check before listing?
sections.html:
Run through these before a listing goes live.

  • Look up your parcel on the Broward appraiser's site and confirm the exemptions shown are ones you still qualify for.
  • Confirm the current year's bill is paid or will be paid at closing.
  • Make sure any renters or other uses that could end homestead are reflected correctly.
  • Ask the closing agent how deed stamp tax and recording will be handled.
  • If you have a payment plan or deferral, ask the tax collector what happens on sale.

Fort Lauderdale's wider Broward market also includes many condos and rentals. With a 54.1 percent owner-occupied rate, a good share of sellers are investors, so the rental and tangible tax questions matter for them too.

sections.h2: Can a Fort Lauderdale owner defer or spread out the bill?
sections.html:
State law offers a homestead tax deferral through Form DR-570, filed with the tax collector by March 31 after the assessment year. It covers taxes above 5 percent of household income, or all taxes when household income is under $10,000, and an owner 65 or older who is a permanent resident may defer the portion above 3 percent.

An installment prepayment plan requires an application to the tax collector by May 1 of the assessment year, and partial payments before the delinquency date are up to the collector's discretion. Many Broward owners simply wait for the TRIM notice in August, which previews the proposed bill, then budget for the November discount.

sections.h2: What happens to taxes when I sell a Fort Lauderdale house?
sections.html:
Your homestead exemption stays with you, so the buyer must file separately, and the title agent prorates the year's bill.

The appraiser states that sellers' exemptions do not carry over beyond the sale year, so the buyer must file their own application. An unpaid balance after April 1 becomes a certificate candidate. Broward uses the standard statewide deed rate, and deeds are recorded at the county Recording Office, 115 S. Andrews Ave, Room 114, Fort Lauderdale, 954-831-4000, open 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

sections.h2: Can I move my Save Our Homes benefit if I buy elsewhere?
sections.html:
Yes, within limits. Portability lets Save Our Homes savings follow you to a new Florida homestead, provided it is set up within three years of the old one's abandonment.

Broward notes that you must first apply for a new homestead and that the portability application is prompted automatically when your information shows a prior exemption. The appraiser says a homestead exemption itself never transfers between properties.

faqs.q: When are Fort Lauderdale property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are sent in November and payable that month at a 4 percent discount, shrinking each month through February. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1.

faqs.q: Where is homestead filed for a Fort Lauderdale address?
faqs.a: File with the Broward County Property Appraiser, online or at its office, by March 1. Call 954-357-6830 with questions.

faqs.q: Does Fort Lauderdale have its own tax assessor?
faqs.a: No. Broward's property appraiser assesses all property in the county, including inside the city limits.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my value in Fort Lauderdale?
faqs.a: Yes, by petition after the August notice, handled through Broward's Value Adjustment Board.

faqs.q: Does renting a homestead cost the exemption?
faqs.a: Possibly. The appraiser warns that owners who no longer qualify must report it by March 1 or face back taxes, a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest.
